      collapsed: false

params:
  metaprogram_metrics_file: NULL
  k_metrics_file: NULL

  cv_background_file: NULL

  n_top_genes: 200
  seed: 2026
---

This report compares the metaprogram sets generated from a single group across a range of k values.
Each k value is a number of metaprograms: the number of clusters specified during hierarchical clustering of NMF programs to define metaprograms.
The optimal k is the k value selected from this range.
It is distinct from the cNMF k, the number of NMF programs found within each library.

## Set Up

```{r}
# helper function for plotting permutation results
# plots metric or score background points with observed values in color on top as sina plot
plot_permutation_results <- function(background_df, observed_df, x_axis, y_axis){

  ggplot(background_df, aes(x = {{ x_axis }}, y = {{ y_axis }})) +
    ggforce::geom_sina(
      color = "gray",
      alpha = 0.1
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = observed_df,
      aes(
        x = {{ x_axis }},
        y = {{ y_axis }},
        color = is_significant
      ),
      size  = 3,
      shape = 18  # diamond
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "red", `FALSE` = "blue")) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)
    )

}
```

```{r setup}
#| message: false
#| echo: false

library(ggplot2)

# Set default ggplot theme
theme_set(
  theme_bw() +
    theme(
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", linewidth = 0.5),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)
    )
)

# define options for tables
options(DT.options = list(
  scrollX = TRUE,
  scrollY = "400px",
  scrollCollapse = TRUE,
  paging = FALSE,
  searching = FALSE
))

# the sina and beeswarm plots are jittered, so set a seed to keep the report reproducible
set.seed(params$seed)

# cutoffs applied by `calculate-optimal-k.R`
# they are repeated here so they can be shown on the plots and must match the values used there
sig_value <- 0.05
correlation_cutoff <- 0.5
coherence_cutoff <- 0.1
```

```{r}
# make sure all inputs were provided and exist
input_files <- list(
  params$metaprogram_metrics_file,
  params$k_metrics_file,
  params$neff_background_file,
  params$specificity_background_file,
  params$cv_background_file,
  params$optimal_k_file
)

stopifnot(
  "All input files from the calculate optimal k script must be provided" = !any(sapply(input_files, is.null)),
  "Some or all input files do not exist" = all(file.exists(unlist(input_files)))
)
```

```{r}
# metrics for each metaprogram within each metaprogram set
# only metaprogram sets that were not excluded are included
mp_metrics_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$metaprogram_metrics_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

# summarized metrics and the normalized rank of each metric for each metaprogram set
# any values of k that were excluded due to low library diversity are included here with no metrics
k_metrics_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$k_metrics_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

# metric backgrounds and score background used to assess significance of the observed metrics
neff_background_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$neff_background_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
specificity_background_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$specificity_background_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
cv_background_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$cv_background_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

# the optimal value of k, reported as a number
optimal_k <- readr::read_lines(params$optimal_k_file) |>
  as.numeric()

# an empty file or a file without a number means no optimal k was chosen
stopifnot(
  "The optimal k file must contain a single number of metaprograms" = length(optimal_k) == 1 && !is.na(optimal_k)
)
```

```{r}
# `n_metaprograms` holds the number of metaprograms as a numeric, which makes every plot treat it as a continuous axis
# it is converted to a factor here so that it is plotted as a discrete axis, with the levels in numeric order
k_levels <- sort(unique(as.numeric(k_metrics_df$n_metaprograms)))

as_k_factor <- function(df) {
  dplyr::mutate(df, n_metaprograms = factor(n_metaprograms, levels = k_levels))
}

mp_metrics_df <- as_k_factor(mp_metrics_df)
k_metrics_df <- as_k_factor(k_metrics_df)
neff_background_df <- as_k_factor(neff_background_df)
specificity_background_df <- as_k_factor(specificity_background_df)
cv_background_df <- as_k_factor(cv_background_df)
```

```{r}
# set figure heights based on if we have the smaller range of numbers of metaprograms (5-15)
# or the larger range (5-25)
total_k <- dplyr::n_distinct(mp_metrics_df$n_metaprograms)
if (total_k <= 12) {
  dynamic_fig_height <- 10
} else {
  dynamic_fig_height <- 20
}
```

```{r}
# report any excluded metaprogram sets that were removed before calculating metrics
excluded_k <- k_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::filter(is_excluded) |>
  dplyr::pull(n_metaprograms)

if (length(excluded_k) > 0) {
  knitr::asis_output(
    glue::glue(
      "
      The following values of k have at least one metaprogram with only one spectra and were removed from this analysis:
      {paste0(excluded_k, collapse = ', ')}
      "
    )
  )
}
```


## Library diversity

Metaprograms should be representative of a diverse set of libraries.
This section will summarize the proportion of libraries found in each metaprogram.

```{r}
# display total libraries
# this is the number of unique ids that contribute cell scores
total_libraries <- max(k_metrics_df$total_libraries, na.rm = TRUE)

knitr::asis_output(
  glue::glue("The metaprograms explored here are comprised of **{total_libraries} libraries**.")
)
```


### Proportion of libraries

Here each dot is a metaprogram and the value indicated is the proportion of total **libraries** represented by NMF programs in that metaprogram.
The dotted line indicates 10% which may help identify any metaprograms with a low representation of libraries.

```{r}
ggplot(mp_metrics_df, aes(x = n_metaprograms, y = proportion_of_libraries)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm() +
  labs(
    x = "Number of metaprograms (k)",
    y = "Proportion of total libraries \n contributing to each metaprogram"
  )  +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.1, linetype = "dashed")
```


### Normalized effective library count

Here we will look at the normalized effective library count or Hill number of order 1.
This is calculated by taking the exponential of Shannon's entropy and represents the effective number of common or abundant libraries.
Here we are looking for a number close to the total possible libraries in that metaprogram.
The values are normalized by the total number of libraries in the metaprogram such that values close to 1 indicate all libraries are equally abundant.
Note that every unique ID in the input samplesheet is treated as a separate library, even if more than one library comes from the same sample.

To determine if the observed effective library count is not due to random chance, we performed permutation testing.
The NMF programs assigned to each metaprogram were shuffled while preserving the total number of NMF programs assigned to each metaprogram.
After shuffling, the normalized effective library count was calculated to create a metric background.

The observed value was compared to the metric background to get an empirical p-value, producing a single p-value for each metaprogram within a metaprogram set.
The below plot shows both the metric background in gray and the observed value for each metaprogram.
The observed values are colored in red if they are significantly greater than the metric background.


```{r}
#| fig.height: !r dynamic_fig_height
#| fig.width: 15

# the plotting function colors points by `is_significant`
neff_obs_df <- mp_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::select(n_metaprograms, metaprogram, eff_number_norm, is_significant = neff_is_significant)

plot_permutation_results(neff_background_df, neff_obs_df, metaprogram, eff_number_norm) +
  facet_wrap(vars(n_metaprograms), scale = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    y = "Normalized effective library count",
    x = "Metaprogram",
    color = "significant"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14)
  )
```

We then can identify the percentage of metaprograms in each metaprogram set that have a significant normalized effective library count.
This is used to identify the optimal value of k in the final section.

```{r}
k_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::filter(!is_excluded) |>
  dplyr::select(n_metaprograms, neff_sig_number, neff_sig_proportion) |>
  DT::datatable(colnames = c("Number of metaprograms", "Number of metaprograms with significant effective library count", "% of metaprograms with significant effective library count")) |>
  DT::formatPercentage("neff_sig_proportion", 2)
```

## Maximum metaprogram correlation

Metaprograms should be unique and non-redundant.
Therefore we expect them to have low correlation to other metaprograms in the same metaprogram set.

Here the pairwise correlation of gene weights across all metaprograms in each metaprogram set was calculated.
The plot then shows the maximum metaprogram correlation, the highest correlation of each metaprogram with any other metaprogram in the same metaprogram set.
Metaprograms with a maximum metaprogram correlation > `r correlation_cutoff` are considered redundant.
The number of metaprograms above this cutoff is used to determine the optimal value of k.


```{r}
ggplot(mp_metrics_df, aes(x = n_metaprograms, y = max_correlation)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(aes(color = correlation_is_passing)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "red", `TRUE` = "black")) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of metaprograms (k)",
    y = "Maximum metaprogram correlation",
    color = glue::glue("Maximum metaprogram correlation less than or equal to {correlation_cutoff}")
  )
```

```{r}
k_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::filter(!is_excluded) |>
  dplyr::select(n_metaprograms, num_passing_correlation, proportion_passing_correlation) |>
  DT::datatable(colnames = c(
    "Number of metaprograms",
    glue::glue("Number of metaprograms with maximum metaprogram correlation less than or equal to {correlation_cutoff}"),
    glue::glue("% of metaprograms with maximum metaprogram correlation less than or equal to {correlation_cutoff}")
  )) |>
  DT::formatPercentage("proportion_passing_correlation", 2)
```


## Coherence

Metaprograms should show coherence, meaning the NMF programs that comprise the metaprogram are more similar to each other than to the NMF programs in other metaprograms of the same metaprogram set.
To measure this, we calculated the correlation of each NMF program to all other NMF programs.
We then calculate the difference in medians between the distribution of correlation of NMF programs within a given metaprogram and between that metaprogram and the other metaprograms in the same metaprogram set, indicated as "coherence" throughout this report.

Metaprograms with coherence <= `r coherence_cutoff` are likely to represent noise and are flagged as low coherence.
They are not removed from the metaprogram set; any low coherence metaprograms in the optimal k are listed at the end of this report.

```{r}
ggplot(mp_metrics_df, aes(x = n_metaprograms, y = median_difference)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(aes(color = coherence_is_passing)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "black")) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of metaprograms (k)",
    y = "Metaprogram coherence",
    color = glue::glue("Coherence > {coherence_cutoff}")
  )

```

Increasing the number of metaprograms may stop improving metaprogram coherence beyond a certain point.
We therefore make an elbow plot showing the median coherence for each metaprogram set and find the elbow.

```{r}
# the median coherence for each metaprogram set, only for the metaprogram sets that were compared
coherence_elbow_df <- k_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::filter(!is_excluded)

ggplot(coherence_elbow_df, aes(x = n_metaprograms, median_coherence)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    x = "Number of metaprograms (k)",
    y = "Median coherence"
  )
```

The elbow is identified with a modified version of the [kneedle algorithm](https://raghavan.usc.edu/papers/kneedle-simplex11.pdf).
Here we only find one global maximum rather than a set of local maxima.
k values greater than the elbow indicate no substantial gain of coherence over lower k values.

```{r}
elbow_value <- coherence_elbow_df |>
  dplyr::filter(is_coherence_elbow) |>
  dplyr::pull(n_metaprograms)

knitr::asis_output(
  glue::glue("**Number of metaprograms corresponding to the elbow: {elbow_value}**")
)
```

## Gene set specificity

After generating each metaprogram set, the top `r params$n_top_genes` genes based on gene weights were extracted from each metaprogram.
Over-representation analysis was then run using `clusterProfiler::enricher()` function on these `r params$n_top_genes` genes.

Any gene sets with an adjusted p value less than or equal to `r sig_value` are considered significant.
Good metaprograms should have at least one significant gene set.

The table below shows the total number of metaprograms with at least one significant gene set in each metaprogram set.

```{r}
k_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::filter(!is_excluded) |>
  dplyr::select(n_metaprograms, num_metaprograms_with_genesets, proportion_metaprograms_with_genesets) |>
  DT::datatable(colnames = c("Number of metaprograms", "Number of metaprograms with at least 1 significant gene set", "% of metaprograms with at least 1 significant gene set")) |>
  DT::formatPercentage("proportion_metaprograms_with_genesets", 2)
```


Metaprograms should be biologically distinct and annotated by a unique set of gene sets.
This means gene sets should be significant in as few metaprograms as possible, ideally only one metaprogram.
For each gene set, we calculated gene set specificity using the following formula:

$$1 - \frac{\text{# of metaprograms the gene set is significant in}- 1}{\text{total # of metaprograms} - 1}$$

A score of 1 indicates the gene set is unique to a single metaprogram, while a score of 0 indicates it is shared across all metaprograms.

We then take the mean specificity across all gene sets and all metaprograms in a single metaprogram set.
Metaprograms with no identified gene sets are not considered in this calculation.

To determine if this value is greater than what would be observed by random chance, we generated a metric background by shuffling the gene sets assigned to each metaprogram, keeping the number of gene sets consistent with the observed distribution and recalculating the mean specificity.
When shuffling the gene sets, each gene set was weighted based on the number of metaprograms in which the gene set was considered significant.

The below plot shows the observed mean gene set specificity and the associated metric background for each metaprogram set.
Any metaprogram sets with a significant mean gene set specificity are indicated in red.

```{r}
gss_obs_df <- k_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::filter(!is_excluded) |>
  dplyr::select(n_metaprograms, overall_geneset_specificity, geneset_specificity_significant) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    is_significant = geneset_specificity_significant == 1
  )

plot_permutation_results(specificity_background_df, gss_obs_df, n_metaprograms, overall_geneset_specificity) +
  labs(
    y = "Mean gene set specificity",
    x = "Number of metaprograms (k)",
    color = "significant"
  )
```


## CV of cell scores

The gene weights for the top `r params$n_top_genes` genes are used to calculate a cell score for each cell in every library in the group.
This is done by taking the dot product of the gene weights and quantile-normalized counts in each cell.

Good metaprograms should show variation in the cell scores across the cells of the libraries in the group.
To measure variation, we will use the coefficient of variation (CV) of cell scores, which is the standard deviation of the cell scores divided by their mean across all cells.

Here we compare the observed CV of cell scores to a score background to determine if a metaprogram shows significantly more variation compared to random chance.
The score background was constructed by shuffling the gene identifiers for each metaprogram in the gene by metaprogram matrix to create shuffled metaprograms.
This ensured that both the weights for each metaprogram and the relationship of genes across metaprograms were retained.
After shuffling, the top genes were extracted, and the cell scores were re-calculated.
This produces a unique score background distribution for each metaprogram.

```{r}
#| fig.height: !r dynamic_fig_height
#| fig.width: 15

cv_obs_df <- mp_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::select(n_metaprograms, metaprogram, score_cv, is_significant = cv_is_significant)

plot_permutation_results(cv_background_df, cv_obs_df, metaprogram, score_cv) +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(n_metaprograms),
    scales = "free_x",
    ncol = 4
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Metaprogram",
    y = "CV of cell scores",
    color = "Significant"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14)
  )
```

The below table shows the total percentage of metaprograms with a significant CV of cell scores in each metaprogram set.

```{r}
k_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::filter(!is_excluded) |>
  dplyr::select(n_metaprograms, num_significant_cv, proportion_significant_cv) |>
  DT::datatable(colnames = c(
    "Number of metaprograms",
    "Number of metaprograms with significant CV of cell scores",
    "% of metaprograms with significant CV of cell scores"
  )) |>
  DT::formatPercentage("proportion_significant_cv", 2)
```

## Combining metrics to identify the optimal value of k

The above metrics are combined to define the optimal value of k.
Each metric has a single number reported for each metaprogram set on a 0-1 scale where 1 indicates a better metaprogram set.
The values included are:

* `Effective library count`: Proportion of metaprograms with a normalized effective library count significantly greater than the metric background (p less than or equal to `r sig_value`).
* `Maximum metaprogram correlation`: Proportion of metaprograms with a maximum metaprogram correlation less than or equal to `r correlation_cutoff`.
* `Coherence`: Value indicating if the number of metaprograms is at, above, or below the elbow point for coherence.
The metaprogram set at the elbow is prioritized and assigned a value of 1.
Metaprogram sets below the elbow will be 0.5 and those above the elbow will be 0.
* `Gene set specificity`: Binary value indicating if the overall gene set specificity is significantly greater than the metric background (p less than or equal to `r sig_value`).
Metaprogram sets that are significant will be 1 and those that are not significant will be 0.
* `CV of cell scores`: Proportion of metaprograms with a CV of cell scores significantly greater than the score background (p less than or equal to `r sig_value`).

For each metric, each metaprogram set is ranked, assigning the same rank to any metaprogram sets with the exact same value for a specific metric.
The rank is normalized by the total number of metaprogram sets compared so that the scale is still 0-1, where 1 indicates a better metaprogram set.
The optimal value of k is the number of metaprograms with the highest average rank.

```{r}
# the rank columns of the k metrics table, in the order they are shown in the heatmap
# the names are used as the row labels, so they are defined here with the rest of the plotting code
rank_columns <- c(
  "Effective library count" = "rank_effective_library_count",
  "Maximum metaprogram correlation" = "rank_correlation",
  "Coherence" = "rank_coherence",
  "Gene set specificity" = "rank_gene_set_specificity",
  "CV of cell scores" = "rank_coefficient_of_variation",
  "Mean rank" = "mean_rank"
)

# selecting with the named vector labels each row of the heatmap, with one column per number of metaprograms
# make sure the numbers of metaprograms appear in the correct order
rank_mtx <- k_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::filter(!is_excluded) |>
  dplyr::arrange(n_metaprograms) |>
  dplyr::select(n_metaprograms, dplyr::all_of(rank_columns)) |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("n_metaprograms") |>
  as.matrix() |>
  t()
```

```{r}
# define a color scale
col_fun <- circlize::colorRamp2(
  breaks = c(0, 0.75, 1),
  colors = c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B")
)

# make the heatmap
ht <- ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap(
  rank_mtx,
  name = "Value",
  col = col_fun,
  # don't cluster and preserve our ordering
  cluster_rows    = FALSE,
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  # Split last row into its own section
  row_split = c(rep("Metrics", nrow(rank_mtx) - 1), "Mean rank"),
  row_gap   = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"),  # gap size between the two sections
  # Labels
  row_names_side    = "left",
  column_names_side = "bottom",
  row_names_gp      = grid::gpar(fontsize = 10),
  column_names_gp   = grid::gpar(fontsize = 10),
  column_names_rot  = 90,
  # Cell appearance
  rect_gp = grid::gpar(col = "white", lwd = 2), # white cell border
  border  = FALSE, # no border around the whole thing
  # Legend
  heatmap_legend_param = list(
    title          = "Value",
    title_position = "leftcenter-rot", # rotate title on left
    legend_height  = grid::unit(4, "cm"),
    at             = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
    labels         = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1")
  ),
  # Axis labels
  row_title      = "Metric",
  row_title_side = "left",
  row_title_gp   = grid::gpar(fontsize = 11),
  column_title      = "Number of metaprograms",
  column_title_side = "bottom",
  column_title_gp   = grid::gpar(fontsize = 11),
  # Square cells: set a fixed size per cell
  cell_fun = NULL,
  width  = grid::unit(ncol(rank_mtx) * 0.8, "cm"),  # 0.8 cm per column
  height = grid::unit(nrow(rank_mtx) * 0.8, "cm")   # 0.8 cm per row (same as width = square)
)
```

```{r}
#| fig.width: 10

# now render the heatmap for the report
ComplexHeatmap::draw(ht, heatmap_legend_side = "right")
```


```{r}
# find any metaprograms in the optimal k that have low coherence
low_coherence_mps <- mp_metrics_df |>
  dplyr::filter(!coherence_is_passing, n_metaprograms == optimal_k) |>
  dplyr::pull(metaprogram)
```

```{r}
# compile text based on if there are any metaprograms with low coherence
main_text <- glue::glue(
  "**The optimal value of k for this group is: {optimal_k}**"
)

coherence_text <- glue::glue(
  "For this metaprogram set, {length(low_coherence_mps)} metaprogram(s) do not pass the minimum coherence of {coherence_cutoff}. "
)

if (length(low_coherence_mps) > 0) {
  # paste the metaprograms into a single string so the line isn't repeated for each metaprogram
  coherence_text <- glue::glue(
    "{coherence_text}
    This includes {paste0(low_coherence_mps, collapse = ', ')}."
  )
}

knitr::asis_output(
  glue::glue(
    "
    {main_text}

    {coherence_text}
    "
  )
)
```
